properties.w: The sultanates of Anjouan, Mohéli and Grande Comore (and Mayotte, until France took it in 1841).
French trading towns, held by Britain from 1793 to 1816, apart from 1802–03.
Founded in 1771 where the Landak joins the Kapuas (shown approximately).
Portugal held the coast and, through its estates (prazos), the Zambezi valley; African kingdoms ruled the interior.
The Khmer kingdom, under Siamese and Vietnamese overlordship.
The Sinhalese kingdom of the island's hill country, ruled from Kandy. The British, who held the coast from 1796, took it in 1815.
Ruled by the Karamanli pashas, in name for the Ottoman sultan, until 1835.
Freetown and its peninsula, settled by freed slaves from 1787 and run by the Sierra Leone Company until it became a crown colony in 1808.
The Empire's many smaller states, shown together. The Empire was dissolved in 1806.
Maratha states under the Peshwa at Pune: Scindia, Holkar, the Bhonsles of Nagpur and the Gaekwads of Baroda. Scindia held Delhi, where the Mughal emperor lived under his protection.

properties.n: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

properties.w: Spain's by treaty since 1778; its settlers left in 1781, and the Bubi people held the island.
Claimed for Britain by James Cook in 1775; no one lived there, but sealers came.
Penang, which the East India Company took from the sultan of Kedah in 1786; the strip of mainland opposite (Province Wellesley) was added in 1800.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1795 to 1818; the Dutch traded it to Britain for good in 1824.
A French colony, held by Britain from 1794 to 1802.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1800 to 1803 and from 1807 to 1816.
The Dutch posts on Sumatra's west coast around Padang, held by Britain from 1795 to 1819.
The Dutch spice islands of Ambon and Banda, with Buru, Seram and the islands to the south-east, taken by Britain in 1796 and handed back in 1803 after the Peace of Amiens.

Ruled from Batavia: the Dutch state took over the Dutch East India Company's possessions on 1 January 1800. Shown with the Javanese kingdoms it held as vassals: Banten (with its pepper lands of Lampung, in Sumatra), Yogyakarta and Surakarta.
French islands, held by Britain from 1793 to 1802.
An Ottoman province, occupied by Napoleon’s army from 1798 until it surrendered in 1801.
Fur-trading posts of the Hudson's Bay and North West companies, as Cliopatria draws them. First Nations held the land around them.
The East India Company's land, shown with Hyderabad, Mysore and Travancore: states under its protection that kept their own rulers.
Spain's claim reached far north of the land it held; much of it was held by Indigenous nations such as the Comanche.
The Hudson's Bay Company's charter territory, around its trading posts; First Nations held most of the land.
Britain's claim to eastern Australia. Its settlements were around Sydney; Aboriginal nations held most of the land.
Spain's viceroyalty, drawn with Chile, which was run on its own from 1798. Spain's claim to Patagonia was not held: Mapuche and Tehuelche nations ruled the south.

properties.n: State of Grão-Pará and Rio Negro

properties.w: Returned to France in secret in October 1800 (Treaty of San Ildefonso); Spain went on running it until 1803, when France sold it to the United States.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1799 to 1802 and again from 1804 to 1816.

Prince Nuku drove out the Dutch-backed sultan in 1797 and ruled Tidore with British support until his death in 1805; the Dutch took it back in 1806. Shown without the coasts and islands of New Guinea that its sultans claimed.
A French colony run by Toussaint Louverture, who had ended slavery there; he took the Spanish east of the island in 1801, and it won independence as Haiti in 1804.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1796 to 1802.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1796 to 1802.
A Dutch colony, held by Britain from 1796 to 1802.

properties.n: British Settlements on the Bay of Honduras
Colony of St Vincent and the Grenadines

properties.w: A kingdom ruled by the Jadeja Raos from Bhuj (shown approximately). It came under British protection by a treaty of 1816.
The Ahom kings ruled the Brahmaputra valley from the 13th century until Burma conquered it in 1817–21; Britain took it in 1826 (shown approximately).
The coast Britain took from the Dutch in 1796, a crown colony from 1802. The Kingdom of Kandy held the hill country until 1815.
